title: Ok but not really what I expected
text:
Ok but not really what I expected. I really wanted to like this thermometer. It had what looked like a lot of good features and I had wanted to try a Bluetooth thermometer for a while. Initially, it looked good. It comes with the thermometer, a charging base, and a charging cord. It doesn't come with a charger, but we have those all over the place.

The first odd thing I noticed is that according to the instructions it must charge for 20 minutes every time you use it. Initially, I thought this was a showstopper because I've been using an electronic thermometer for several years and it is always ready to work. When I used it for the first time, I realized that in most cases there is at least 20 minutes of prep time, and you don't need to put the thing in the meat right away. So, that's annoying but not a showstopper. What is really goofy is that you can't even set it up until you charge it for 20 minutes. The charging base shows red when it is charging and green when it is done, but it also goes back and forth. When I was charging it for the first real use, I looked over and it was green. Then I went to get it a few minutes later and it was red.
The biggest issue is the app that comes with it. It's very primitive and doesn't look like it has a lot of options. You can choose one of the "BBQ" menu items and in most cases, it will then give you the option of various degrees of doneness. It works ok but is really limited in terms of connection. It says you can connect up to 165 feet, and that is only if you have the lid open on the grill or oven. I don't know a lot of people who use a grill with the top open, and I know of no one who uses an oven with the door open. It does say in the description that if you close the lid of the grill you will get about 20 feet before it disconnects. I'd say that is pretty accurate but means that you have to stay pretty close to the grill, and that's not why anyone would get a wireless remote thermometer. I suspect the battery is very weak which is why you have to charge it all the time and the weak signal is the reason it doesn't work over 20 feet. This may be fine if you are in a small kitchen and using it with the oven, but normally I move around a bit.
The worst thing about it is that it won't turn off. I used it and two days later it's still running even though I thought I ended it. Evidently, you have to go in and actually force it to stop. This is definitely a security issue and a battery usage issue and just a horrible customer service issue.
Overall, I can't give this device more than 3 stars. The app can be updated, and hopefully this will happen, but the weak signal is not something that will be fixed and the need to charge it every time you use it is another limitation. I expect a wireless thermometer to be pretty simple to operate and have an app that is easy to use. This has neither of those basic features and having no way to close the app is a definite security issue.
